commitResults.messageTitle: Support common student and guardian names
commitResults.messageBody:
Student and guardian names reject Unicode letters and punctuation used
in valid real-world names.

Accept letters from any language, internal apostrophes and hyphens,
and supported Singapore name connectors. Preserve names in storage and
treat canonically equivalent Unicode spellings consistently during
duplicate checks.

Allow the same characters in name searches, document the accepted
forms, and cover model, parser, command, search, and storage behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept formatted phone numbers
commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject editstudent and editlesson with identical details
commitResults.messageBody:
editstudent and editlesson previously reported success when supplied
values produced an unchanged record. This suggested that data changed.

Reject identical edits by raising a command error before model
replacement, so they do not trigger a save. Continue accepting commands
where at least one resulting field is different.

Update command and logic tests, the User Guide, and the Developer Guide
to cover rejected identical edits and partially changed edits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve v1.4 student phone data
commitResults.messageBody:
Loading stored students with the strict v1.5 phone rule skips records
whose phone numbers were valid in v1.4. Enrolments for those students
are then dropped during recovery.

Use the legacy phone rule for stored student and guardian numbers while
keeping strict validation for addstudent and editstudent input. Add a
load-and-save regression test covering legacy numbers and enrolments,
and document the upgrade behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle long formatted phone input safely
commitResults.messageBody:
The repeated-group phone regex can overflow the stack when validating
thousands of digit groups. This can prevent startup for stored data and
can fail typed commands without a useful error.

Replace regex matching with an iterative character scan. Add model,
parser, and storage tests using 3,000 groups to verify validation does
not overflow and typed input returns a normal parse error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Shorten the student phone validation message
commitResults.messageBody:
The student phone constraint message is too wide for the status box, so
users cannot see the complete requirements.

Reduce the message to 71 characters while retaining the accepted local,
+65, and international formats. Add a length regression test using the
status-box limit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow lessons to run past midnight
commitResults.messageBody:
A lesson's end time had to be later than its start time, so a late
lesson such as Friday 2200 to 0100 could not be recorded.

Read an end time earlier than the start time as ending on the next
day, with the lesson belonging to the day it starts on. Only an end
time equal to the start time is still rejected. Swapped start and end
times are therefore no longer reported as a mistake.

Update the developer guide and the lesson model notes to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add addlesson and deletelesson commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Closes #52. addlesson n/NAME d/DAY st/START_TIME et/END_TIME adds a
weekly lesson, and deletelesson INDEX deletes the lesson at that index
in the displayed lesson list, keeping its students.

A day is one of mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat or sun in any letter
case, and a time is exactly four digits from 0000 to 2359. The rules
for a lesson's name and times stay in Lesson, whose own messages are
shown. A duplicate lesson is rejected even when a filter hides it.

Tests also cover that deleting a lesson or a student removes only its
own enrolments, both in the model and in the saved file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test minute precision of lesson start and end times
commitResults.messageBody:
The time check in Lesson's constructor was only exercised with seconds
on the start time, so its branches for nanoseconds and for the end
time were never taken.

Cover seconds and nanoseconds on both times.

Shorten the time message, and split the usage messages into lines

commitResults.messageTitle: Show next-day lessons and unenrolled students in lesson results
commitResults.messageBody:
Swapped times such as st/1800 et/1600 are accepted as a lesson that
ends the next day, but the result gave no hint of it. Add
Messages.format(Lesson), which marks such lessons "next day" as lesson
cards do, and use it in addlesson and deletelesson.

deletelesson also removed enrolments silently. It now lists the
students it unenrolled on a second line, so a tutor knows whom to
re-enrol after deleting the wrong lesson.

Also lower-case "Deleted lesson" and end the duplicate lesson message
with a full stop. Document deletelesson in the user guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn about clashing lessons when adding a lesson
commitResults.messageBody:
addlesson still adds a lesson whose time overlaps an existing one, as
the tutor may mean to, but now names the clashing lessons on a second
line of the result. Clashes are found among all lessons, including
those hidden by a lesson filter.

Lesson#overlaps compares weekly time ranges, so a lesson past midnight
covers the start of the next day, including Sunday into Monday.
ReadOnlyAddressBook#getClashingLessons leaves out the lesson's own ID,
so editlesson can reuse it.

Document the warning in the user guide, UC03, the manual testing
appendix and LessonModel.md.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find students by phone number
commitResults.messageBody:
A tutor often gets a call or message from a number they have not
saved, and needs to know which student or family it belongs to.

findstudent now takes p/ followed by digit sequences. It matches
students whose own or guardian's phone number contains any of them.
As with n/ and gn/, a student must match every prefix given.

Name keywords are now checked against the rule in Name instead of a
separate copy of it, so search stays in step if that rule changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Assert lesson durations are positive and reject null clash queries
commitResults.messageBody:
A lesson's duration is positive because the constructor rejects an
end time equal to the start time, which overlaps relies on. Assert
it, and make getClashingLessons reject a null lesson even when there
are no lessons to compare against.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give name and phone keyword parsing their own methods
commitResults.messageBody:
The return statement of FindStudentCommandParser#parse built all
three keyword lists inline, one of them with a lambda, mixing levels
of abstraction. Move the name and phone rules into parseNameKeywords
and parsePhoneKeywords.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document how lesson clashes are found
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a Developer Guide section with a sequence diagram of addlesson
finding clashing lessons, how overlaps handles lessons past midnight,
and the design alternatives considered.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark next-day lessons without duplicating lesson formatting
commitResults.messageBody:
Messages#format(Lesson) repeated the formatting in Lesson#toString,
and the next-day check was written out in both it and
LessonUiFormatter. Add Lesson#endsNextDay, build the message on
Lesson#toString, and mark the lesson "(next day)" as the lesson cards
do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app with Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Java disables assertions by default, so the asserts in the code were
never checked when the app was started with ./gradlew run. Gradle's
test task already enables them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update Model and Storage class diagrams
commitResults.messageBody:
The diagrams were drawn before the lesson model was implemented. They
show classes that do not exist (TutorBook, UniqueStudentList,
UniqueLessonList, LessonName, EnrolmentList, JsonAdaptedGuardian) and
have each student hold its lessons.

Let's redraw them to match the code. AddressBook holds lists of
students, lessons and enrolments, and each Enrolment links a student
UUID to a lesson UUID. The storage side mirrors this with a
JsonAdaptedEnrolment list, and stores guardian details as fields of
JsonAdaptedStudent.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for finding students by a phone number as typed
commitResults.messageBody:
findstudent p/9123 4567 split the number into two keywords and listed
every student whose phone contained either half, and p/+65 9123-4567
was rejected. The tests expect p/ to take one number, ignoring spaces
and hyphens, and to match a stored number when a country code is in
front of it.

The help window also listed findstudent twice, once without p/. The
test expects it once, with the new p/PHONE format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find students by a phone number as typed
commitResults.messageBody:
findstudent p/ now takes one phone number, or part of one, written as it
often is: spaces and hyphens are ignored, and a leading + is allowed. A
full number with a country code in front, as shown by a caller ID,
matches the stored number it ends with, so p/+65 9123 4567 finds
91234567. Before, p/9123 4567 listed every student whose phone
contained 9123 or 4567.

Remove the old findstudent line without p/ from the help window, and
update the usage message, the User Guide and the Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for warning about clashes when editing a lesson
commitResults.messageBody:
addlesson warns when a new lesson overlaps others, but editlesson could
move a lesson onto another's time with no warning. Its result also
showed a lesson past midnight without the (next day) marker. The tests
expect editlesson to warn as addlesson does, including about lessons
hidden by a day filter, and expect both commands to share one formatter
for the warning.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn about clashing lessons when editing a lesson
commitResults.messageBody:
editlesson now checks the edited lesson against every other lesson, as
addlesson does, and adds the same warning line to its result when they
overlap. The lesson is still edited. Lessons hidden by a day filter
count, and the lesson's own old times do not, since getClashingLessons
skips its ID.

Move the warning's wording from AddLessonCommand to
Messages#formatClashWarning so both commands share it. The editlesson
result now also marks a lesson past midnight (next day).

Update the User Guide, the clash-warning section, the user story, UC09
and the manual test cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy the User Guide's lesson commands
commitResults.messageBody:
deletelesson was documented twice, once among the lesson commands and
once among the old person commands, with different details. Keep one
section, among the lesson commands, with the details of both.

The command summary listed Add lesson and Delete lesson twice; keep one
row each.

The addlesson section did not mention the name rules, when a lesson
counts as a duplicate, the clash warning, that adding clears the lesson
filter, or the (next day) marker in results. Add them, with an example
of a clash warning.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for short numbers and pasted phone fragments
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha testing found two gaps in the phone search. A stored number as
short as 567 matched any full number ending in 567, such as +65 9123
4567. And p/-4567, copied from the end of 9123-4567, and p/+ 65 9123
4567 were rejected, though they contain only the characters the error
message allows.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match a country code only in front of a full number
commitResults.messageBody:
A search number now matches a stored number it ends with only if the
stored number has at least seven digits and the extra digits in front,
the country code, are at most three. A stored 567 no longer matches
+65 9123 4567 or +1 555 0567.

Also accept a search that starts with a hyphen or has a space after the
+, such as p/-4567 copied from 9123-4567, or p/+ 65 9123 4567.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for reading pasted Unicode spaces as spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
Text copied from a PDF, a web page, a messaging app or a caller ID can
carry no-break, narrow or ideographic spaces, or invisible zero-width
characters. Commands with them failed with "Unknown command." or an
error quoting text that looked valid, e.g. findstudent with a pasted
+65 9123 4567. The tests expect them to be read as plain spaces, and
invisible characters to be dropped.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read pasted Unicode spaces as spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
AddressBookParser now passes the command through
StringUtil#normalizeSpaces before parsing. It turns every Unicode space,
such as the no-break space U+00A0 or the ideographic space U+3000, into
a plain space, and drops zero-width characters and byte order marks.
So a command copied from the User Guide PDF, or a phone number copied
from a caller ID, works as if typed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for marking next-day lessons in enrolment results
commitResults.messageBody:
enrol, unenrol and liststudents l/ name the lesson in their results,
but showed a lesson that runs past midnight as, e.g., Fri 2300-0100,
without the (next day) marker that addlesson and deletelesson use.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark next-day lessons in enrolment results
commitResults.messageBody:
Format the lesson with Messages.format(Lesson) in the results and
errors of enrol and unenrol, and in the result of liststudents l/, so a
lesson past midnight reads Late Physics (Fri 2300-0100) (next day), as
it does after addlesson and deletelesson.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for a clearer equal-times message
commitResults.messageBody:
The error for an end time equal to the start time also said times must
have minute precision, which users cannot get wrong since they type
times as HHmm. The tests expect that error to name only the equal times,
and a separate message for times with seconds.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name only the equal times in the lesson time error
commitResults.messageBody:
addlesson n/Math d/mon st/1600 et/1600 now reports "End time must not
be the same as start time." instead of also saying times must have
minute precision. Seconds can only come from code, so that check keeps a
message of its own.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for naming unknown prefixes in errors
commitResults.messageBody:
A prefix a command does not take, such as gp/ in findstudent or p/ in
addlesson, was read as part of the value before it. The error then
blamed that value: findstudent n/aiden gp/123 said search keywords must
be alphanumeric, and addlesson ... et/1800 p/123 said times must be
four digits. The tests expect an error naming the prefix and listing
the ones the command takes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for full day names and times with colons
commitResults.messageBody:
addlesson, editlesson and listlessons rejected d/monday and d/tues, and
st/16:00 even though lesson cards show times as 16:00. The tests now
expect any start of a day's name with at least three letters, and times
as HHmm or HH:mm. Inputs that stay invalid, such as d/weds, replace the
old examples.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name unknown prefixes in addlesson and findstudent errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Before tokenizing, addlesson and findstudent now look for a word that
looks like a prefix, such as gp/ or e/, but is not one they take. The
error names it and lists the prefixes the command does take, e.g.
"findstudent takes only n/, gn/ and p/, not gp/.", instead of blaming
the value it would have been read into.

A slash right after a prefix, as in n/Math/Science, is still part of
the value and is checked by that value's rules. Other commands can call
ArgumentTokenizer#verifyNoUnknownPrefixes in the same way.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept full day names and times with colons
commitResults.messageBody:
A day may now be its full name or any start of it with at least three
letters, in any case, so d/monday, d/tues and d/Thurs work alongside
d/mon. A time may be HHmm or HH:mm, matching how lesson cards show
times; with a colon the hour may drop its leading zero, as in 9:30.

Three-letter starts of day names are all different, so no input matches
two days. Times without a colon still need four digits, so a typo such
as 100 for 1000 is not quietly read as 01:00.

Update the usage messages, the User Guide and the manual test cases that
used d/tues and d/monday as invalid days.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for slash words in lesson names
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha testing found that the unknown-prefix check took any word ending
in a slash for a prefix: addlesson n/Sec 3 Physics/Chem ... said
"addlesson takes only n/, d/, st/ and et/, not Physics/." The tests
expect such words to be left to the lesson-name rule, while TutorReach's
prefixes in any case, and one- or two-letter words like e/, are still
named.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for accepting weds as Wednesday
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha testing found d/weds rejected while d/tues and d/thurs work.
"weds" is as common as those but is not the start of "wednesday".
The invalid-day examples in the tests now use "funday" instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for wrapping long result messages
commitResults.messageBody:
A clash warning or a list of unenrolled students can be wider than
the result box. The tests expect the box to wrap such messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Leave slash words that are not prefixes to the value's rules
commitResults.messageBody:
A word ending in a slash is now taken for a mistyped prefix only if it
is one of TutorReach's prefixes in any case, such as N/ or GP/, or one
or two lower-case letters, such as e/ and t/ from AddressBook-Level3.
Other words, such as Physics/ in Physics/Chem or A/ in A/E Math, are
checked by the lesson-name rule as before, so the error names the real
problem.

Add CliSyntax.TUTORREACH_PREFIXES for the prefixes that the commands
take.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept weds as Wednesday
commitResults.messageBody:
parseDay now also reads "weds", in any case, as Wednesday, next to any
start of a day's name with at least three letters. Update the User
Guide's day rule and the invalid-day examples in the manual tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap long messages in the result box
commitResults.messageBody:
The result box did not wrap text, so at the default window width a
warning about several clashing lessons, or the list of students
unenrolled from a deleted lesson, ran past the right edge. The user had
to scroll sideways to read it.

Wrap the text instead. Messages that are still too tall for the box get
the usual vertical scroll bar.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for an oversized deletelesson index
commitResults.messageBody:
deletelesson 99999999999 said "Invalid command format!", though the
index is well formed and only out of range, which past PE testers
report as a wrong error message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report an oversized deletelesson index as invalid
commitResults.messageBody:
When the index is a positive whole number too large to parse, such as
99999999999, deletelesson now says "The lesson index provided is
invalid.", as it does for any index beyond the displayed list. Other
malformed indices still get the usage message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document how findstudent matches students
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a Developer Guide section on findstudent, with an activity diagram
of how StudentContainsKeywordsPredicate decides a match, how the parser
reads pasted text and phone numbers, and the design choices behind
reading p/ as one number and matching country codes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for clearer duplicate, double-booking and long-lesson results
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha testing and past PE reports point to three gaps in the lesson
commands:
- "This lesson already exists" did not say which lesson, even when a
  day filter hid it.
- enrol said nothing when the student already attended a lesson at an
  overlapping time, though double-booking a student is the mistake the
  clash warning exists to catch.
- Swapped or one-sided times, such as editlesson 1 st/1900 on a
  1600-1800 lesson, silently made a lesson over 20 hours long.

The tests expect the duplicate error to name the lesson and say how to
show it if hidden, enrol to warn about the student's clashing lessons,
and addlesson and editlesson to warn when a lesson runs past midnight
for more than 12 hours.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name duplicates and warn of double-booked students and long lessons
commitResults.messageBody:
- A duplicate lesson is now rejected with "This lesson already exists:
  <lesson>", plus how to show it when the day filter hides it. Both
  addlesson and editlesson use Messages#formatDuplicateLesson, and
  AddressBook#hasLesson reuses ReadOnlyAddressBook#findDuplicateOf.
- enrol warns, after enrolling, which of the student's own lessons
  clash with the new one.
- addlesson and editlesson warn when a lesson runs past midnight for
  more than 12 hours, which almost always means swapped times, such as
  editlesson 1 st/1900 on a 1600-1800 lesson.

Update the User Guide, the clash-warning section, UC04 and the manual
tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document how deletelesson removes a lesson
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a Developer Guide section on deletelesson, with a sequence diagram
of how the command, the model and the address book remove the lesson
and its enrolments and reset a student filter that referred to it, and
the design choices behind keeping students and resetting that filter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the new duplicate check in the addlesson diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
AddLessonCommand now finds the duplicate through
ReadOnlyAddressBook#findDuplicateOf so that it can name it. Update the
sequence diagram and its description to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show a clash warning in the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Past PE testers often report too few screenshots in User Guides. Add
one of the main window after an addlesson that clashes with another
lesson, under the addlesson examples.

commitResults.messageTitle: Size the performance requirement to what was measured
commitResults.messageBody:
NFR 2 promised commands under 1 second with 1000 students and 200
lessons, but data-changing commands take about 0.7-0.9 s at that size
on a fast laptop, leaving no margin for slower ones. At 300 students and
100 lessons they take at most about 0.2 s, more than an independent
tutor needs, so state that size instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the performance requirement
commitResults.messageBody:
A requirement with a time limit gives testers a target to measure, and
data-changing commands slow down as the data grows (see #112). Drop the
performance requirement from the list of non-functional requirements
and renumber the rest.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the requirement to show the command format in every error
commitResults.messageBody:
Not every error shows the command format: "Unknown command." and the
field rules, such as the name rule, do not. Drop the requirement rather
than promise more than the error messages give.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use the code's class names in the Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Logic section, the proposed undo/redo section and their diagrams
named TutorBook, TutorBookParser and VersionedTutorBook, which do not
exist in the code. Rename them to AddressBook, AddressBookParser and
VersionedAddressBook, and the matching methods, and re-render the
architecture, delete, parser, commit and undo/redo diagrams.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say that student names take only English letters
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide said names may contain only "letters" or "alphanumeric
characters", but accented letters, as in José, are rejected, so a tester
could report the guide as wrong. State that only English letters, digits
and spaces are accepted, and name the symbols that are not, such as the
/ in s/o.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the AddressBook commands from the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide still described the add, list, edit, find and delete
person commands, which the app no longer has, and its introduction,
quick start, command format notes and FAQ still spoke of AB3 contacts.
Remove those sections, the placeholder archiving section and the add,
edit and delete summary rows, and describe TutorReach with its own
commands instead. Point the download link at our releases page.

The quick start adds a student who is not in the sample data, so the
example does not fail as a duplicate.

The find and list summary rows sit next to the findstudent row that
another pull request changes, so they are removed there instead.

Also write "an AddressBookParser" in the Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the find and list rows from the command summary
commitResults.messageBody:
The command summary still listed the AddressBook find and list
commands, which the app no longer has. Remove them here, beside the
findstudent row this pull request changes, so that the rest of the
User Guide cleanup in #121 does not conflict with it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Launch the released jar by its name in the quick start
commitResults.messageBody:
The quick start now links to our releases page, whose jar is
tutorReach.jar, but it still said to run addressbook.jar.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the unenrol diagram and use the code's class names
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide's unenrol section linked images/UnenrolSequenceDiagram.png,
which did not exist, so readers saw a broken image. The section and the
diagram source also still named TutorBook and TutorBookParser, which are
not in the code.

Use AddressBookParser and an ab:AddressBook lifeline in the diagram, as
the edit-student diagram does, and render it. In the text, name
ReadOnlyAddressBook#isEnrolled(), as the enrol section does, and
AddressBook.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use an addstudent example that works on the sample data
commitResults.messageBody:
The example addstudent n/Aiden Tan gn/Tan Mei Ling gp/91234567 adds a
student who is already in the sample data, so on a fresh launch it fails
with "This student already exists". It appeared in the User Guide's
addstudent section and command summary, the README, the command's usage
message and the Developer Guide's first manual test.

Use Marcus Lim, who is not in the sample data and differs from the quick
start's student, and adjust the duplicate manual tests to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that the sample data has no AddressBook persons
commitResults.messageBody:
The sample data still adds AB3's six people (Alex Yeoh and others).
TutorReach never shows them, but they are written to the data file,
where a user editing it would find them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the AddressBook persons from the sample data
commitResults.messageBody:
Stop adding AB3's six sample people, which TutorReach never shows, so
a new data file holds only the sample students. The persons list in the
file is now empty.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace AddressBook names left in messages and the icon
commitResults.messageBody:
Users still met AB3's name: clear said "Address book has been
cleared!", exit said "Exiting Address Book as requested ...", the
addstudent usage message and two User Guide sections said "address
book", and the window used AB3's icon.

Name TutorReach, or students and lessons, instead, and replace the icon
with a TutorReach monogram.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test unknown prefixes in addstudent and editstudent
commitResults.messageBody:
addstudent and editstudent read a prefix they do not take as part of
the value before it, so editstudent 1 n/Aiden x/abc reports an invalid
name and editstudent 1 x/abc an invalid command format. Expect the error
to name the unknown prefix, as addlesson and findstudent already do.

The names Kumar s/o Ravi and Siti d/o Ahmad must keep getting the name
rule's error, not an unknown s/ or d/ prefix, and findstudent n/kumar s/o
should report s/o as an invalid keyword.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name unknown prefixes in addstudent and editstudent errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Run ArgumentTokenizer#verifyNoUnknownPrefixes() in addstudent and
editstudent, as addlesson and findstudent do, so editstudent 1 n/Aiden
x/abc reports the unknown x/ instead of an invalid name.

Skip the name connectors s/o, d/o, a/l and a/p, in any letter case, so
a name such as Kumar s/o Ravi still gets the name rule's error rather
than an unknown s/ prefix. findstudent n/kumar s/o now reports s/o as
an invalid keyword for the same reason.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn that clear cannot be undone
commitResults.messageBody:
clear deletes every student and lesson at once, with no confirmation
and no undo, and clear 1 does the same since extra text is ignored. The
User Guide did not say so, and PE testers report such commands as data
loss. Add a caution to the clear section.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add regression tests for inputs PE testers try
commitResults.messageBody:
Past PE reports show testers copying every User Guide example, typing
near-duplicates and invalid indexes, and editing the data file by hand.
TutorReach handles these, so add tests that keep it that way:

- UserGuideExamplesTest runs each User Guide example on the sample data.
- DuplicateEntryTest rejects near-duplicate students and lessons, added
  or created by editing, and reloads accepted data without skipping any.
- InvalidInputTest rejects zero, negative, fractional and huge indexes,
  out-of-range values and commands on empty lists without a crash or a
  change to the data or the data file.
- HandEditedDataFileTest loads hand-edited data files: invalid records
  are skipped with a warning and a backup, and an unreadable file leaves
  saving disabled and the original untouched.

The tests run commands through LogicManager and a real data file, as a
tester's input does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that cards show renamed students and lessons
commitResults.messageBody:
A card that keeps showing old details after an edit is a common High
severity PE report. Check that the lesson card shows a renamed student,
and that the student card shows a renamed and moved lesson.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #121 from randomwish/tidy-lesson-user-guide
commitResults.messageBody: Wrap long results and complete the lesson documentation

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #120 from randomwish/warn-clash-on-edit
commitResults.messageBody: Improve lesson input, results and warnings

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #118 from randomwish/search-phone-as-typed
commitResults.messageBody: Handle pasted text, phone searches and unknown prefixes

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the DG manual tests for launching and listing students
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual tests said to launch by double-clicking the jar, while the PE
has testers run it with java -jar, and expected sample lessons, which
the sample data does not have. They also expected liststudents l/1 to
state how many students are shown, but its message names the lesson.

Launch with java -jar tutorReach.jar, the released jar's name, expect
only the sample students, and expect the lesson to be named.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #126 from randomwish/fix-dg-manual-tests
commitResults.messageBody: Correct the DG manual tests for launching and listing students

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for reading command words in any letter case
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha testing (#130) found that ADDLESSON and AddLesson were rejected
as unknown commands, although the command word means the same in any
case. The tests expect any letter case to give the same command, with
the arguments, such as a lesson name, keeping their own capitals.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read command words in any letter case
commitResults.messageBody:
AddressBookParser now puts the command word in lower case before
choosing the command, so ADDLESSON, AddLesson and addlesson all add a
lesson. Prefixes stay lower case, and an upper-case prefix is still
named as unknown. The User Guide's notes on the command format say so.

Fixes #130

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for finding names regardless of accents and apostrophes
commitResults.messageBody:
Names may contain accented letters and either a straight or a curly
apostrophe, but findstudent n/jose did not find José, and n/O’Connor,
pasted from a document, did not find O'Connor. The tests expect name
keywords to ignore the accents of Latin letters and the apostrophe
style, while names in other scripts, such as Tamil, still match only
as stored.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find names regardless of accents and apostrophes
commitResults.messageBody:
The search predicate now decomposes both the name and the keyword,
drops the combining accents of Latin letters (U+0300 to U+036F) and
makes curly apostrophes straight before comparing them. Marks of other
scripts are kept, since they are part of their letters.

Describe the rule in the User Guide and the Developer Guide, and add
a manual test for it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for naming the missing addlesson fields
commitResults.messageBody:
A missed space before a prefix, as in st/1600et/1800, hides that
prefix inside the value before it, but addlesson only answered
"Invalid command format!" without saying what was wrong. The tests
expect the error to name the missing fields, in the order of the
command format, and to keep the plain usage message when no field is
given at all.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the missing fields in addlesson errors
commitResults.messageBody:
When some but not all of n/, d/, st/ and et/ are given, the error now
starts with, for example, "Missing et/END_TIME. Each prefix must have
a space before it." before the usage, so a user who missed a space
sees which prefix was not read. Add the case to the manual tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Write times as HHMM in the time error
commitResults.messageBody:
The error for an invalid time said "HHmm or HH:mm", the pattern letters
of Java's formatter, while the User Guide and the usage message write
HHMM and HH:MM. Use the User Guide's form so that the two agree.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the lesson rules in the guides
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha testing found four places where the guides described the lesson
rules wrongly:

* The editlesson section and the DG said the long-lesson warning comes
  when a lesson runs more than 12 hours past midnight, and the DG said
  a few hours past midnight give no warning. The warning is for a
  lesson that ends the next day and lasts more than 12 hours in all,
  so 1300 to 0200 warns, as the addlesson section already says.
* The DG said the clash warning is the result's second line. It is the
  last line, after the long-lesson warning if there is one.
* The day rule gave weds as an example of "at least its first three
  letters", but weds is not the start of wednesday. It is accepted as
  an extra abbreviation, so the rule now names it.
* Lesson names may contain /, but a word such as w/ in Chem w/ Lab is
  read as a mistyped prefix and the command is rejected. The command
  format notes now say which words are read as prefixes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix the quick start example, FAQ and command summary
commitResults.messageBody:
The quick start's addstudent example gave Ben Koh's guardian the phone
number 98765432, which the addstudent examples give to Daniel Ng as a
student's own number. Under the phone rules, trying the examples in
order fails, so Ben Koh's guardian now has a number of their own.

The FAQ told users to overwrite "the data file it creates" on the new
computer, but TutorReach writes no data file until the data changes,
and the User Guide never said where the file is. It now says to copy
the data folder, which holds addressbook.json.

The command summary had no row for exit and no clear order. Add the
row and list the commands alphabetically.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the DG manual tests to the current behaviour
commitResults.messageBody:
Three expected results no longer matched the app:

* addstudent n/Marcus Lim p/88887777 now also warns that another
  student has the same name.
* A new lesson is placed in timetable order, not at the end of the
  lessons panel.
* enrol with a student index beyond the list shows "Student index
  exceeds the number of students in the displayed list.", not "The
  student index provided is invalid".

commitResults.messageTitle: Show LogicManager's activation in the lesson diagrams
commitResults.messageBody:
The addlesson and deletelesson sequence diagrams drew :LogicManager
calling execute(m) and receiving r without an activation bar, unlike
the other sequence diagrams in the DG. Activate it for the whole call.

The Logic class diagram's note gave FindCommand, an AddressBook class
that no command word reaches, as an example of XYZCommand. Name
FindStudentCommand instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for confirming clear in any letter case
commitResults.messageBody:
Now that command words are read in any letter case, CLEAR shows the
warning, but CLEAR CONFIRM was still rejected as an invalid format.
The tests expect the confirmation word to be read in any case too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept the clear confirmation word in any letter case
commitResults.messageBody:
clear now compares its argument with "confirm" ignoring letter case,
so the whole command can be typed in any case, as #130 asks for the
command word.
